setting: A short talk in an archaeology class about how Roman aqueducts supplied cities with water.
narrator_intro: Listen to part of a talk in an archaeology class.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Roman cities needed huge amounts of fresh water for drinking, baths, and fountains.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Engineers solved that with aqueducts—channels that carried water from distant springs into town.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Most of an aqueduct ran underground or in covered trenches to keep the water clean and cool.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: The famous arched bridges appear where the route had to cross a valley while keeping a gentle slope.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Gravity did the work: a slight downhill grade moved water for kilometers without pumps.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Inside the city, water reached public baths, street fountains, and sometimes private homes of the wealthy.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Maintenance crews cleared sediment and repaired leaks, because a break could cut supply for days.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Some aqueducts still stand, which tells us how carefully the Romans planned long-distance water systems.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: So when you see those arches in photos, remember they were only one visible piece of a much longer network.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Next time we’ll compare Roman water technology with earlier systems in Greece and the Near East.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: How Roman aqueducts brought water to cities
options.C: Why baths were banned in Rome
options.D: How to dig modern subway tunnels

questions.explanation: The professor explains aqueduct design, gravity flow, and city water use.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing B—he says gravity moved water without pumps.

questions.narrator_text: According to the professor, why did most of an aqueduct run underground or in covered trenches?

options.A: To keep the water clean and cool

questions.explanation: He says covered routes kept water clean and cool.

questions.narrator_text: What made the water move through the aqueduct?

options.A: A slight downhill grade using gravity
options.B: Teams of horses pulling carts of water

questions.explanation: Gravity and a gentle slope moved water for kilometers without pumps.

questions.narrator_text: What does the professor imply about the arched bridges people photograph?

options.A: They were the entire aqueduct system by themselves
options.B: They were built only for decoration in theaters
options.C: They never carried water at all
options.D: They were only the visible part of a much longer water network

questions.explanation: He says the arches were one visible piece of a much longer network.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—he stresses the longer underground route.
